title: CRISPR: Gene Editing Goes Programmable
summary: CRISPR-Cas9 (Doudna/Charpentier, 2012; Nobel 2020) cut DNA at chosen sites using guide RNA.
body:
Synthetic biology engineers life; nanotechnology engineers molecules. Together they promise programmed cells, molecular machines, and DNA as storage — much of it already working in labs.

CRISPR-Cas9 (Doudna/Charpentier, 2012; Nobel 2020) cut DNA at chosen sites using guide RNA. Base editors and prime editors now rewrite single letters. First CRISPR therapies (sickle cell, 2023 FDA approvals) are real medicine.

title: Synthetic Genomes: Writing DNA
summary: JCVI-syn3.
body:
JCVI-syn3.0 (2016): a bacterium with the smallest known genome — 473 genes, all essential (plus unknowns). Writing genomes from scratch tests what life minimally requires.

title: DNA Origami

body:
